note: Minispiel „Das Relaispult“ im Dolmetschergang des Palais (Kapitel 3, Konrad; TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE 12.8, owner minigames_r7_relay). Nüchterner Ton, nie strafend, keine Ausrufezeichen. Keine Mikrofonnummern, keine Uhrzeiten oder Tagesordnungsnummern, nichts zu Anlage C (das Protokollrätsel bleibt unberührt); Elena kommt nicht vor (Kabine 2 bleibt namenlos). Die Reden sind sinngemäß auf Deutsch wiedergegeben. Fundtext in Konrads Stimme (explore.veltrava.hall.relay.*). Allgemeine Knöpfe: mg.common.* in de_minigames.json.

strings.mg.relay.title: The relay console
strings.mg.relay.subtitle: The commission’s sound engineer has to go down to the hall; a microphone is crackling. “You can read wiring diagrams? Then mind the channels for me for a few minutes.”
strings.mg.relay.instruction: Plug each channel into the source currently speaking its language: the floor itself or the booth marked with that language. If a lag runs into the yellow: Yellow – slower. Into the red: Red – brief pause.
strings.mg.relay.rows.head: Channels
strings.mg.relay.r1.title: Winter timetable across the border bridge
strings.mg.relay.r1.note: Calm pace. Channel EN is still on the floor sound – the observers need booth 3.
strings.mg.relay.r1.done: Down below, people nod. Nobody looks up at the console.
strings.mg.relay.r1.t1: “We come to the winter timetable across the border bridge. I invite requests to speak.”
strings.mg.relay.r1.t2: “We propose running the grain trains across the bridge at night: at twenty-two ten, twenty-three forty and zero fifty hours.”
strings.mg.relay.r1.t3: “No objection – provided the brake tests take place before the bridge and not in the station.”
strings.mg.relay.r1.t4: “Then we shall record the three night paths. I thank the delegations.”
strings.mg.relay.r2.title: Food trains in winter
strings.mg.relay.r2.note: Brisker, with figures. Keep an eye on the lags.
strings.mg.relay.r2.done: In booth 2, someone briefly raises a hand: everything got through.
strings.mg.relay.r2.t1: “For the winter we expect four hundred and twenty tonnes a week – sixty-one wagons, spread over three nights.”
strings.mg.relay.r2.t2: “Sixty-one wagons in three nights? Only one train at a time may cross the bridge. We ask for four nights.”
strings.mg.relay.r2.t4: “No objection. But clearance at the bridge stays with the Reichsbahn, as before.”
strings.mg.relay.r2.t5: “Clearance is a matter for the commission. We will discuss it tomorrow in the technical committee.”
strings.mg.relay.r3.title: Point of order: the bridge closure
strings.mg.relay.r3.note: Quick changes and interjections. Re-plug while the chair is still giving the floor.
strings.mg.relay.r3.done: The chair reaches for the bell.
strings.mg.relay.r3.t1: “We are behind schedule. I ask for brief contributions on Tuesday’s bridge closure.”
strings.mg.relay.r3.t2: “The closure on Tuesday hits the milk trains from the north: six trains of two hundred churns each.”
strings.mg.relay.r3.t5: “Wednesday, then. For the milk every day is the same – not for the children.”
strings.mg.relay.r3.t7: “Wednesday, then. The session is suspended for ten minutes.”
strings.mg.relay.summary.fail_ratio: Only {p}% understood. The chair has the passage repeated.
strings.mg.relay.summary.fail_lost: Booths lost the thread: {n}. The chair has the passage repeated.
strings.mg.relay.status.intro: About to begin. Set the channels right now.
strings.mg.relay.status.announce: The floor goes to: {who} ({lang}). Re-plug now.
strings.mg.relay.status.far_behind: Booth {n} can barely keep up – Red.
strings.mg.relay.status.yellow: Yellow lamp: the speaker slows down.
strings.mg.relay.status.yellow_ignored: All booths are keeping up. The speaker merely glances up.
strings.mg.relay.status.red: Red lamp: the speaker pauses, the booths catch up.
strings.mg.relay.status.red_ignored: Nobody is far behind. The chair shakes his head.
strings.mg.relay.fail.lost: Booth {n} has lost the thread. Its channel goes silent for a few seconds.
strings.mg.relay.hint.plug: Tip: The guide lights now show the right socket. Whoever speaks the speaker’s language gets the floor; everyone else gets the booth marked with their language right now.
strings.mg.relay.hint.lamp: Tip: Yellow as soon as a needle runs into the yellow – not only once it’s in the red. Booths on relay fall behind faster with figures.
strings.mg.relay.hint.announce: Tip: While the chair is giving the floor, nothing counts yet. Re-plug during that pause – the top line shows who speaks next.
strings.mg.relay.beat.1: The chair rings. The session is suspended.
strings.mg.relay.beat.2: The interpreter from booth 1 leans out of the door, headphones round her neck.
strings.mg.relay.beat.3: “Thank you. You pressed the lamps before we had to ask.”
strings.mg.relay.beat.3.lost: “Thank you. We floundered a few times. You saw it every time.”
strings.mg.relay.beat.4: “Ten minutes’ break. The only ones in which everyone here speaks the same language.”
strings.mg.relay.beat.6: “None at all. One drinks coffee and says nothing.”
strings.mg.relay.solved: The engineer comes back up the stairs and takes over the console again.
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.relay.title: The relay console
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.relay.prompt: Help out at the relay console
strings.explore.veltrava.hall.relay.text: Sixteen sockets, three booths, two lamps. For a few minutes I pulled plugs and pushed them in while, down below, they argued about milk trains, and nobody in the hall noticed that a draughtsman was at the console. “Good engineering goes unnoticed,” says the engineer. I have always said the same about my drawings. Afterwards the interpreter from booth 1 rubbed her ears for a long time.
